title: Compound Assignment: %=
concept: %= updates a variable to the remainder when divided by a value — shorthand for x = x % y.
why: %= is useful for wrapping values around (like clocks), cycling through ranges, and keeping numbers within bounds.
syntax_ref: x %= y;  // Same as: x = x % y
tips: `x %= n` keeps x in the range `0..n` (wraps around)
`%=` works with Int only — no Float64 remainder-assign
% by zero will cause a runtime error — always check divisor
common_mistakes: Using `%=` with Float64 — it's for Int only
Dividing by zero: `x %= 0` causes an error at runtime
Assuming `%=0` preserves the value — it wraps to 0..n-1, not 0..n
